correctness.rationale: Every depth-d point type is a visible exact cycle period c<=d with q^c color words or an all-distinct d+1 term window with q^(d+1) color words. The visible profiles force one cycle per short necklace; distinct long profiles force q^(d+1) long vertices; a de Bruijn tour achieves equality. Every optimal model canonically labels its long vertices by unique word-arcs, giving a de Bruijn local transition matching without cycles of length at most d; conversely all such systems yield optimizers. A repeated length-d graph state in a short permutation cycle forces shorter color period and repeated arc, contradiction, so short cycles are exactly simple directed graph cycles. Inclusion–exclusion over their compatible prescribed local pairs gives E_(q,d). Short necklace rotational stabilizers and rigid long vertices give the labeled formula. The bundled verifier independently checks 25 bounded cases, returning VERIFY_OK 25; those cases are not used as a proof for arbitrary q,d.

value.rationale: The least finite colored-permutation model simultaneously realizing every depth-d one-variable atomic profile is a natural resource invariant for finite-model testing and saturation. A sharp closed-size formula and all-optima structural classification provide the precise budget; a nontrivial q=2,d=2 boundary exhibits a genuine multi-long-cycle optimizer missed by single de Bruijn word constructions. The all-parameter inclusion–exclusion and automorphism factor give reproducible exact isomorphism and labeled censuses, without claiming an artificial isolated numerical slice.
